questions.prompt: A runner completes one full lap of a 400 m circular track. What are the distance and displacement?
questions.explanation: Distance is the total path length (400 m). Displacement is the straight-line vector from start to finish; after one full lap the runner returns to the start, so displacement = 0.

options: Distance can be negative; displacement cannot
Displacement can be negative; distance cannot
Both distance and displacement can be negative
questions.explanation: Distance is a scalar and is always non-negative (it is a path length). Displacement is a vector and can be negative depending on the chosen positive direction.

questions.prompt: A car drives 6 km north, then 8 km east. What is the magnitude of its displacement?
questions.explanation: The two legs are perpendicular, so the displacement is the hypotenuse: sqrt(6^2 + 8^2) = sqrt(100) = 10 km. The 14 km option is the total distance travelled.
